title: Universal Fidelity Law for Linear-Optical Entangling Gates
abstract: Imperfect photon sources degrade the performance of interference-based linear-optical entangling gates. We derive a universal fidelity law for these gates in terms of two standard source metrics: Hong-Ou-Mandel visibility and second-order coherence. We model the multiphoton component as an arbitrary overlap between noise and signal photons. While different values of the signal-noise overlap produce different error structures, associated with different physical platforms, all result in the same fidelity law. We test the model on our actively synchronized CNOT-gate experiment and against published results across different platforms, with no free parameters. This framework turns source characterization into a unified benchmark for photonic quantum computing.
summary: This paper derives a universal fidelity law for linear-optical entangling gates that accounts for noise from imperfect photon sources. By analyzing contributions from single, pair, and three-photon emissions, the authors show that the gate fidelity can be predicted using only measurable quantities like HOM visibility and second-order coherence. This provides a unified benchmark for advancing photonic quantum computing.
main_problem: The performance of interference-based linear-optical entangling gates is degraded by imperfect photon sources, necessitating a universal fidelity law.
main_result: The authors derive a universal fidelity law for these gates expressed solely in terms of measurable source metrics (HOM visibility and second-order coherence), independent of the specific physical platform.
method: The methodology involves deriving the two-qubit density matrix using coincidence operators and analyzing contributions from single, pair, and three-photon emission events.
model_or_system: The system is an interference-based CNOT gate implemented using linear-optical elements and single-photon sources (e.g., SPDC). The analysis models the gate operation using creation operators incorporating temporal wavepackets.
key_observables: Gate Fidelity (F), Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) visibility (V), and second-order coherence ($g^{(2)}(0)$).
important_parameters: Photon indistinguishability ($\eta$), signal-noise overlap parameter ($M_{sn}$), and emission-event weights ($w_x, r_x$).
main_assumptions: The initial derivation uses an approximation valid for at most two photons, though the framework extends to three-photon events. The universal law relies on expressing fidelity via measured quantities to absorb platform-specific noise origins.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the CNOT gate components and defines parameters like $\eta$ and $g^{(2)}$. Other figures/tables detail the coincidence matrices ($\sigma$) for different noise types and the derived visibility relations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the source of error (imperfect sources) to deriving the general fidelity expression by analyzing multi-photon contributions, culminating in the universal law that relates fidelity to measurable source parameters.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial, platform-agnostic benchmark for characterizing and optimizing photonic quantum computing hardware, directly linking fundamental source statistics to gate performance.
